1 طَخَا اللَّيْلُ , [aor.
1َ2ُ3َ ,] inf. n. طَخْوٌ and طُخُوٌّ; and طَخَى [of which the aor. is app.
1َ2ِ3َ , and the inf. n. طَخْىٌ]; The night was, or became, dark. (TA. [The former of these verbs, with the latter of its inf. ns., is mentioned by Golius as on the
authority of J; but I do not find it in either of my copies of the S.]) ―
-b2- And طَخَى, inf. n. طَخْىٌ, He was, or became, foolish, stupid, or unsound [as though obscured] in intellect or understanding. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
